events.note: Authored for credential-evidence#243 (Group D, D2 handoff) from the contract claims instagram-app-secret/instagram-app-secret-carrier-in-code-exchange, instagram-app-secret/instagram-app-secret-carrier-in-long-lived-exchange, read on 2026-10-06 in this repository, without any scanner output. Carrier existence is provider-documented; the span and the value policy are project policy. Not an independent review.

Decided 2026-10-06 by the sole maintainer (Milo Kang, milocosmopolitan, repository owner) for credential-evidence#243. Question: Is the client_secret value of an Instagram token exchange a credential when no format is stated and its relation to the Meta app secret is open? Options: Flag the field and parameter values; or leave the Case a draft until the relation to the Meta app secret is settled. Decision: Flag the value of client_secret in the two documented carriers. No expectation on a bare value and none on the Instagram App ID. Reason: Both carriers are named, the page requires server-side use because the request includes the secret, and the relation question changes attribution, not whether the value is a credential. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone under the solo-maintainer period (ADR 0020): not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). Recorded by an AI agent on the owner's explicit instruction of 2026-10-06 (complete redact-secret#1228, #1229 and #1230 before the next release; Cases for these groups are authored maintainer-only, as in Batch 2).
events.dissent: No dissent was raised. The strongest counter-argument, recorded because the rule asks for one: The value may be the same secret as the Meta app secret, in which case one family owns it and this Case duplicates an expectation; the pages state no format, so a position-only rule can flag a non-secret.
events.reversingEvidence: A Meta statement that the Instagram App Secret and the Meta app secret are one value, or of the secret's format, or a second maintainer's retro-review that disputes it.
